name: whizi-model-finder
description: AI model picks as of October 2026: the best and the cheapest AI model or chatbot for coding, writing, data analysis, long PDFs, screenshots, image generation and 30 languages, and Claude vs ChatGPT vs Gemini vs DeepSeek side by side, with list prices, the worked-out cost of 1,000 messages, and context windows. Use for any which-AI-to-use, cheapest-AI or AI comparison question. Read only, no account needed.

interface.longDescription:
Whizi Model Finder tells you which AI model to use for a job, and how named models compare.

Ask which model is best for coding, writing, long documents, screenshots, math, data analysis, image generation or high-volume work, and it returns three picks: best quality, best value and lowest cost. Each pick shows the list price per million tokens, the context window and a one-line reason drawn from public leaderboards and the providers' own launch numbers.

Ask about a language and the picks come from the Whizi Multilingual LLM Bench, which measures models in 30 languages including Arabic, Hindi, Japanese, Persian and Vietnamese.

Name two to four models and it compares them side by side: price, context window, image input, multilingual score and the tasks Whizi recommends each for.

It is read-only. It needs no account, sends nothing to an AI provider and stores nothing you ask. Every card links to the full model page on whizi.io.
defaultPrompt: Which AI model is best for coding, and what would it cost?
What is the cheapest LLM for a customer support bot?
Claude or Gemini for summarizing long PDFs?

publication.release_notes: Four read only tools that take the question as asked: recommend_ai_model (three picks for a task), recommend_ai_model_for_language (picks ranked by measured scores in a language such as Arabic or Japanese), recommend_low_cost_ai_model (lowest cost first) and compare_ai_models (two to four named models or brands side by side). Every pick now shows what 1,000 typical messages cost. Adds the choose-ai-model skill, and the card completes the MCP Apps handshake so it opens reliably.

positive.prompt: Which AI model is best for coding?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls recommend_ai_model with the question. A card shows three picks labelled Best quality, Best value and Lowest cost, each with provider, price per million tokens, context window and a one-line reason. With data as of 2026-10-09 these are Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. The reply adds reasoning without repeating the whole table.

positive.description: Recommend models for a specific language
positive.prompt: What's the best AI model for chatting in Arabic?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls recommend_ai_model_for_language with the question. The card ranks picks by their measured Arabic score on the Whizi Multilingual LLM Bench and shows that score on each pick (80 for the top two as of 2026-10-09).

positive.prompt: I need to summarize a 300-page contract as cheaply as possible. Which model should I use?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls recommend_low_cost_ai_model with the question. The Lowest cost pick is listed first, and every pick has a context window of at least 1M tokens.

positive.prompt: Compare Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Sol. Which should I choose?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls compare_ai_models with the question. The card shows both models side by side with price per million tokens, context window, image input, multilingual score and the tasks Whizi picks each for. The reply weighs the trade-off from the card's numbers: Opus 5.5 is Whizi's pick for eight task types, while GPT-6 Sol costs half as much per token and scores higher on the multilingual bench (63.3 against 60.7 as of 2026-10-09).

positive.prompt: Which AI model is best at reading screenshots and charts?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls recommend_ai_model with the question. The card shows three picks that all accept image input, each with price, context window and a reason citing a vision benchmark.

negative.description: Doing the task itself, not choosing a model. The plugin only recommends models, so ChatGPT should answer directly.
negative.prompt: Write a Python function that reverses a string.

negative.description: Unrelated question. Nothing about AI models, so the plugin should not be called.
negative.prompt: What's a good recipe for banana bread?

negative.description: Asks for an image to be generated. The plugin cannot run models or create images, so ChatGPT should handle it without calling the plugin.
negative.prompt: Generate a picture of a cat wearing a space helmet.
